reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Pooled sovereign AI against great-power dominance
themes.definition: Rejection of AI decisions being monopolised by two powers or a few private actors, with proposals for states to have their own model and compute capabilities and to pool resources for a shared open-source frontier model.
themes.inclusion: Include passages about avoiding dependence on dominant AI powers/companies, sovereign compute or model capacity, or pooled open-source models.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general calls for regulation without a dependence or concentration framing.
themes.boundary_cases: Mention of a national frontier model framed as independence counts here; framed as national pride only, code AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: There are some who wish to make us believe that only two powers, the US and China, will be taking the decisions.
we must come together to build an open source frontier model, a cutting edge model using all of the calculation capabilities you have pooling them

themes.label: Protecting children from chatbots and platforms
themes.definition: Concern about harms of AI chatbots and digital platforms to children and adolescents, and coalitions for children's rights in the AI era.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on AI or chatbot harms to children, youth mental health, or children's rights in the AI era.
themes.exclusion: Exclude youth skills and education opportunities in AI (AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION).
themes.boundary_cases: Social media age limits without AI mention are borderline; code only when discussed in the AI context of the passage.

examples.quote: Look at the impact chatbots have on our children. This is why, together with Kenya, Spain, Australia, we've built a coalition on children's rights in the era of AI.

themes.label: AI regulation, summits and auditing
themes.definition: Advocacy for AI regulation through international initiatives (GPAI, AI summits, the EU AI Act) and the ability to audit models.
themes.inclusion: Include references to international AI regulation processes, summits, or regulatory acts and model auditing.
themes.exclusion: Exclude security-specific rulemaking on AI in defence or space (AI_SECURITY_ARMS_CONTROL).
themes.boundary_cases: A general exhortation 'not yield on artificial intelligence' without specifics is borderline and may be coded here as a rhetorical governance stance.

examples.quote: we launched the Global Partnership for Artificial Intelligence under the auspices of the OECD to kickstart discussions on the need for regulation
we must hold fast and not yield on artificial intelligence

themes.label: New rules for AI in defence and space
themes.definition: Calls for new rules on AI in outer space, defence and cybersecurity because of national-security consequences.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for rules on AI in defence, space, or security domains.
themes.boundary_cases: Explicit autonomous weapons or targeting discussion should be coded AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.

examples.quote: there are other areas where we must set new rules. AI in outer space, AI and defense and cybersecurity.

themes.label: National frontier model investment
themes.definition: The speaker highlights its own competitive frontier AI model and continued national investment.
themes.inclusion: Include references to the speaker's national AI models, companies, or investment.
themes.boundary_cases: National investment framed as a race among states may also be coded AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: France is proud to have a competitive frontier model

value.rationale: All three passages come from France 2026 and treat AI as a strategic arena: resisting concentration by the US, China and private firms, pooling sovereign compute, regulating and auditing models, protecting children from chatbots, and setting security rules. The ocean/climate passage only closes with a brief AI pivot.
